sentences.text: Nothosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropterygian reptile that lived during the Triassic period, approximately 245 to 228 million years ago. Fossils of this animal are distributed throughout the former Tethys Ocean, ranging from North Africa and Europe to China.
It was a semi-oceanic animal with a lifestyle likely similar to that of modern seals. Nothosaurus was about 4 meters long, possessed long webbed toes, and likely had a fin on its tail.

While some individuals reached about three meters, the species generally grew to a length of about four meters. Nothosaurus possessed very sharp, dagger-shaped teeth that interlocked between the upper and lower jaws, creating a perfect trap for fish.

Some species, such as N. zhangi and N. giganteus, grew larger, reaching up to 5 to 7 meters in length. Nothosaurus was the most common genus in its group, with fossils discovered in widely separated locations including the Netherlands, China, and Spain.
Nothosaurus had a powerful bite capable of holding prey so tightly that few animals could shake free once caught.
Evidence of vivipary, or live birth, was found in seven out of twenty-four studied Nothosaurus specimens.
The fossil taxon Nothosaurus was first described in 1834. The genus was originally described by Hunter in 1834.

The type species of Nothosaurus is N. mirabilis, which was named in 1834 from the Germanic Muschelkalk formation. Several species, including N. marchicus and N. winkelhorsti, have been described from the Lower Muschelkalk in Winterswijk, the Netherlands.
The lost type material of N. schimperi, originally described from Soultz-les-Bains, France, was recently rediscovered and a lectotype was designated.

Nothosaurus could close its mouth with great force, but the muscles required to reopen it were very weak. Well-preserved fossils show that Nothosaurus had webbed feet suitable for both aquatic and terrestrial environments.

Due to their characteristics, Nothosaurus specimens likely spent part of their lives on land, moving over sand and rocks. Nothosaurus likely came ashore to rest, bask in the sun, catch prey in shoreline pools, and reproduce by laying eggs.
Trackways reported from Yunnan, China in June 2014 were interpreted as paddle impressions left by Nothosaurus digging into soft seabed to stir up benthic creatures.
Researchers suggest that vivipary in Nothosaurus may have been an adaptation to increase early survival rates, compensating for high mortality at later life stages.

In 2017, the species N. juvenilis, N. youngi, and N. winkelhorsti were formally reclassified and moved to the genus Lariosaurus. Nothosaurus has numerous synonyms including Chondriosaurus, Conchiosaurus, Dracontosaurus, Dracosaurus, Elmosaurus, Kolposaurus, Menodon, Oligolycus, Opeosaurus, Paranothosaurus, and Shingyisaurus.
